basis_question.text:
Read the following passage:

1. The climate and landscape in Uttarakhand vary greatly with altitude (186 - 7619 m), from the largest glaciers in the higher elevation to the subtropical forests in the lowest elevation.

2. The lowlands along the border of U.P. are covered by the drier Terai-Savanna grasslands, the moist deciduous forest of the Upper Gangetic Plains form the Bhabhar belt. Due to the extensive agricultural practices, most of these lowland forests have been cleared. Snow and bare ice occupy the highest altitudes.

3. This state occupies 53,483 sq. km., (1.63% of India's total land area). Out of 13 districts, Uttarkashi occupies the maximum area of 8039 sq. km., while Champawat covers the minimum area of 1634 sq. km. Uttarakhand experiences four types of seasons, namely, Monsoon (June to September), Post-monsoon (October to November), Cold weather (December to February) and Pre-monsoon (March to May). The normal annual precipitation in the state is 1446 mm. Rain usually starts at the end of April and lasts until September. The monsoon rainfall is 78% of the annual rainfall. This makes the state prone to flood during monsoon. Bageshwar receives the maximum normal annual rainfall (1872 mm). 81% falls of this rainfall occurs in the monsoon season. Haridwar receives the minimum normal annual rainfall (1107 mm).

4. Due to the differences in topographical features, temperatures vary widely. During March and April, temperatures rise until they peak in May and June, when the mean maximum temperature in the southern and valley regions is between 34° and 38°C, and the mean minimum temperature is between 20° and 24°C. Temperatures can reach 42°C in the valleys and southern half of the state and 30°C in two-kilometre-high elevations on some days. Day and night temperatures begin to dip around the end of September and reach the lowest in January and early February. January is the coldest month, with an average maximum temperature of 20°C and an average lowest temperature of 6°C. The mean maximum and mean minimum temperatures range from 10° to 12°C at altitudes of 2 km.

Answer the following questions, based on the passage above:

subparts.answer: The rain in Uttarakhand starts by the end of April and it lasts till September. The monsoon rainfall is 78% of the annual rainfall.

subparts.answer: (D) Bageshwar and Haridwar

subparts.answer: The moist deciduous forest of the Upper Gangetic plains form the Bhabhar belt.

questions.text:
Read the following passage:

1. The Western Ghats, also known as the Sahyadri, form a mountain chain that runs for about 1,600 km along the western edge of the Deccan Plateau, from the Tapi valley in the north to the southern tip of the peninsula. The range passes through six states: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

2. The hills act as a great wall for the south-west monsoon. Moist winds from the Arabian Sea are forced upwards by the slopes, cool, and fall as heavy rain on the western side, where some places receive more than 5,000 mm in a year. The eastern side lies in the rain shadow of the range and is much drier, which is why the landscapes on the two sides differ so sharply. Many of peninsular India's great rivers, including the Godavari, the Krishna and the Kaveri, rise in these hills and flow eastwards.

3. The region covers about 140,000 sq. km., less than 5% of India's land area, yet it shelters more than 30% of the country's species of plants and animals. Its highest peak, Anamudi in Kerala, rises to 2,695 m. Animals such as the Nilgiri tahr and the lion-tailed macaque live nowhere else in the world. In 2012, UNESCO added 39 sites of the Western Ghats to its World Heritage List, recognising their rare natural value.

4. Despite this honour, the forests are under pressure. Mining, expanding plantations, new roads and unplanned tourism have broken the forest into small fragments. Scientists warn that if the loss continues, the rivers that feed millions of people may weaken. Conservationists therefore urge community-based protection of the forests and more responsible tourism.

Answer the following questions, based on the passage above:

subparts.text:
i. Fill in the blank suitably: (1 Mark)
According to paragraph 1, the Western Ghats run from the ________ in the north to the southern tip of the peninsula.
subparts.answer: Tapi valley

subparts.answer: upwards, heavy

subparts.text: iii. Based on the passage, which side of the range is drier? (1 Mark)
subparts.answer: The eastern side (it lies in the rain shadow of the range).

subparts.text:
iv. In the given sentence taken from paragraph 4, select the option that correctly replaces the underlined word, with its most likely Antonym. (1 Mark)
Mining, expanding plantations, new roads and unplanned tourism have broken the forest into small fragments. (underlined word: expanding)
subparts.answer: (C) shrinking

subparts.text: v. 'The Western Ghats are vital for the rivers of peninsular India.' Justify the statement with reference to the passage given above in 30-40 words. (2 Marks)
subparts.answer: Many of peninsular India's great rivers, such as the Godavari, the Krishna and the Kaveri, rise in these hills and flow eastwards. The range also forces the monsoon winds to shed heavy rain on its western side, and the loss of its forests may weaken these rivers.

subparts.answer: (A) Anamudi, Kerala

subparts.answer: It lies in the rain shadow of the range.

subparts.answer: In 2012; 39 sites.

(B) The range passes through five states.
options: (A) The Western Ghats cover less than 5% of India's land area but shelter more than 30% of the country's species.

subparts.answer: (B) - The range passes through six states (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu), not five.

questions.text:
Read the following passage carefully:
1. There was a time when human interference was minimum, the number of wild animals was quite high and there was no problem of their protection or conservation.
2. Due to the irrational use of natural and biotic resources of the Earth in the past, most of the wildlife has been destroyed beyond retrieval. According to an estimate, in India about 200 species of wild animals and birds have become extinct and another 2500 are on the verge of extinction. Some of them are black buck, chinkara, wolf, swamp deer, nilgai, Indian gazelle, antelope, tiger, rhinoceros, gir lion, crocodile, flamingo, pelican, bustard, white crane, grey heron, mountain quail, etc.
3. In India, the Government and NGOs are taking keen interest in protection of wildlife. The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, has several provisions for the conservation of wildlife. As many as 165 game sanctuaries and 21 national parks have been deployed to protect the natural habitat and wild animals. Apart from this, Wildlife Conservation Week is also celebrated from 1st to 7th October every year. But still there is a long way to go in this direction.
4. Preservation of wildlife does not mean a blanket protection to all faunal and floral species; rather it implies a proper, judicious control over the multiplication of plants and animals which interact together to provide a proper environment to man whose very existence is in peril today.
5. It is our urgent duty to protect the natural splendour of ecosystems and to evolve a system of coexistence with every living creature upon the Earth.
[Bar graph (based on IUCN Red List data): Mammals 530, Birds 799, Reptiles 504, Amphibians 632, Fishes 1174, Insects 716, Molluscs 1016, Other Invertebrates 708. See figure.]
Based on your understanding of the passage, answer the questions given below:

subparts.answer: less human interference / bare minimum human interference

I. destroyed

subparts.answer: a. I and II

subparts.text: III. Complete the following analogy correctly with a word/phrase from the passage. (Clue: Just like flowers are in a garden, similarly________ are in the sanctuaries.) Flowers: Garden::________: Sanctuaries
subparts.answer: wildlife

subparts.text: IV. Select the correct option to complete the sentence. Judicious control over the multiplication of plants and animals which provide
subparts.answer: b. proper environment to man

subparts.text:
V. According to the graph, which is the most vulnerable animal species and the least vulnerable from the graph.
I. Birds
II. Insects
III. Fishes
IV. Reptiles
V. Insects
VI. Mammals
VII. Molluses
subparts.answer: III & IV (most vulnerable: Fishes; least vulnerable: Reptiles). Official note: 'Options are incorrectly placed. B is the closest.' i.e. option b.
subparts.note: Option list printed with errors in the paper (as given); graph shows Fishes 1174 highest, Reptiles 504 lowest.

subparts.text:
VI. Assertion (A): Wildlife conservation is essential to maintain a balanced ecosystem and ensure human survival.
Reason (R): The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, and initiatives like sanctuaries and Wildlife Conservation Week aim to protect endangered species and their habitats.
options: A. Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
B. Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
C. (A) is true, but (R) is false.
D. (A) is false, but (R) is true.
subparts.answer: A. Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

subparts.text: VII. List any two examples of Government and NGOs trying to protect the wildlife.
subparts.answer: The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, has several provisions for the conservation of wildlife / 165 game sanctuaries and 21 national parks have been deployed, protecting the natural habitat and wild animals / Wildlife Conservation Week is celebrated from 1st to 7th October every year (any two)

subparts.text: VIII. List one reason why the Government makes certain recommendations for protection of wild animals.
subparts.answer: to protect the natural habitat and wild animals / to keep ecological balance (any one)

subparts.text: IX. What is the main aim of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 in India?
subparts.answer: The main aim of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 is to conserve wildlife by protecting natural habitats and wild animals through provisions such as sanctuaries and national parks.

questions.text: The given double bar graph shows the preferences of children in a school in playing different games over the span of six years. Write an analytical paragraph about the given information.
questions.answer:
The given double bar graph shows the preferences of children in a school in playing different games over the period of six years i.e., from 2014 to 2019.
The graph shows that the highest number of children interested in playing volleyball is in the year 2016 whereas in the year 2019, very less number of children preferred volleyball. The graph shows a hike in the game of volleyball again in the year 2018. The data shows that the preference of people in basketball is almost constant, like in the years 2014, 2017, and 2018 same number of children showed interest in it. Basketball got a slight hike of interested children in the year 2016 but a decline has been seen in it in 2019 which is equal to 2015.
If we observe the graph we can see that childrens preference related to volleyball is continuously changing every year. Although initially 200 children were interested in volleyball in 2014. Then it reached 300 in 2015, the greatest hike of 450 in 2016, but it again declined to 250 children in 2017, it again showed a hike of 400 children in 2018 and the lowest number of children i.e., only 150 in 2019.
Whereas basketball was much preferred in 2014 than volleyball. It shows a decline of 100 children in 2015 but again reached 400 in 2016 and then remained same in 2017 and 2018.
To conclude the data shows that throughout the six years basketball was more preferred in comparison to volleyball. Although data shows that volleyball has got the highest number of interested children in 2016 but the numbers are constantly flickering which reached the lowest and is less preferred by the children in the year 2019 also.

or.text: The given pie charts show percentage of boys of class 12 of two different schools regarding their interest in participation in different quizzes. Write an analytical paragraph describing the given information.
or.answer:
The given pie charts show the data of two schools about the interest of boys in participation in different quizzes.
The most preferred choice of subject by school-1 is maths where 35% students preferred it. Science came second which was preferred by 30% students. The students of school-1 showed equal interest in the quizzes of English and commerce, which shows 10% of participation. For G.K. 15% students from school-1 showed interest. The most preferred subject by school-1 is maths and least ones are English and commerce.
In School-2 the most preferred choice of subject was science which was preferred by 35% students. Maths was the second preferred choice, preferred by 25% students. Next is English with 20% students being interested in it and then commerce where only 10% students preferred it. The least preferred choice by the students of school-2 was G.K. which was preferred by only 5% students.
To conclude we can say that the top choice for both the schools were maths and science with slight variation in numbers. The students of School-2 were least interested in G.K. whereas School-1 had a tie in their least preferred choice which was both commerce and English.

basis_question.text: You are Suyash/Suhani Pandey, the Eco-Club Captain of Kendriya Vidyalaya School, Shripur. You are well aware of the hazards of using plastic bags indiscriminately and want the authorities to ban the excessive use of these bags. Write a letter to the editor of a national daily, drawing attention towards the harm caused by plastic litter. Express your concern over environmental degradation due to plastic waste and request the public to avoid the reckless use of polybags.
basis_question.answer:
To
The Editor
A National Daily
New Delhi

Subject: Harmful effects of plastic bags on the environment

Sir/Madam,

I am Suyash Pandey, the Eco-Club Captain of Kendriya Vidyalaya, Shripur. Through your esteemed newspaper, I wish to draw attention to the serious harm caused by the indiscriminate use of plastic bags. Plastic litter clogs drains, pollutes soil and water, harms animals, and takes hundreds of years to decompose. Despite repeated warnings, people continue to use polybags recklessly, worsening environmental degradation.

I request the authorities to strictly ban excessive use of plastic bags and promote eco-friendly alternatives like cloth and jute bags. I also appeal to the public to act responsibly and reduce plastic usage for a cleaner, healthier future.

Yours sincerely,
Suyash Pandey
Eco-Club Captain

12, Gandhi Nagar

Subject: Growing addiction of teenagers to online games

subparts.text: Describe the physical appearance of Custard the dragon.
subparts.answer: Custard, the dragon had big sharp teeth and spikes on its back that could easily scare anyone away. It had ability to spit fire which made his mouth like a fireplace and thus his nose became a chimney. The toes were so pointed and sharp, that it could cut anything like a daggar.

subparts.text: Fill in the blank with one word. This extract describes the physical appearance of Custard. He carried all the features of ________ that could make him powerful, scary, and brave.
subparts.answer: dragon

subparts.text: Which belief about dragons is in contrast to Custard's behaviour in the extract.
options: a. Dragons are brave and feared.
c. Dragons can become invisible at will.
d. Dragons are soft-hearted and kind.
subparts.answer: (a) Dragons are brave and feared.

subparts.text: Comment on the poet's use of language in these lines.
subparts.answer: The language used in these lines is simple and straightforward. The words and phrases are easy to understand and the poem is written in a conversational tone. Realio and Trulio words are creating poetic effect. This is a humurous poem.

The poet talks about the house as a place of _________.

subparts.answer: The second line uses alliteration - long letters - whereas the last line uses a simile - like a voice into the rooms.

subparts.text: The extract uses 'open' twice, suggesting different meanings. Write the correct meaning with reference to the extract.

basis_question.text: Answer ANY FOUR of the following five questions, in about 50 words each.
basis_question.note: Five 3-mark questions are printed; any four are to be attempted (12 marks).

subparts.text: i. Pranjal seemed to have a different level of enthusiasm compared to Rajvir when they both saw the tree plantation. Justify. (Glimpses of India) [3]
subparts.answer: Pranjal and Rajvir had different levels of enthusiasm when they saw the tea plantation. Rajvir was very excited, as it was his first time seeing such a vast tea garden. He found it beautiful and unique, which made him eager to learn more about tea. On the other hand, Pranjal, who had grown up on a tea plantation, didn't share Rajvir's excitement. For him, the sight of the tea bushes was normal, as he was already used to it. He even mentioned that Assam had many such gardens, and Rajvir would see plenty more. This shows that Pranjal was not as fascinated by the plantation as Rajvir was because it was a part of his daily life.

subparts.text: ii. What would the tiger do in the forest? [3]
subparts.answer: In the forest, the tiger would walk freely without any foundation and terrify the villagers snarling around their houses. The tiger in the wild would be majestic. He would be free and lie under the shades and hunt for prey.

subparts.text: iii. Justify the title of the play The Proposal with reference to the characters and plot. [3]
subparts.answer: The title "The Proposal" is apt because the play revolves around a marriage proposal that sets off a chain of comedic events. The characters - Chubukov, Lomov, and Natalya - are involved in a humorous misunderstanding over property boundaries and Lomov's hesitant proposal to Natalya. The title captures the central theme of courtship and the absurdity that ensues when emotions and egos clash.

subparts.text: iv. Why did Margot and Anne stay with their grandmother? [3]
subparts.answer: Anne and her sister Margot went to Aachen to stay with their grandmother, when their parents emigrated to Holland in 1933.

subparts.text: v. Why does the poet of Fire and Ice hold with those who favour fire? [3]
subparts.answer: The poet takes side with those who believe that the world will be destroyed by fire. Frost connects fire with desire. Desire indicates all kinds of greed and lust. According to the poet, desire is powerful and would bring a quick end. He believes that when a human's emotions overpower him, destruction is greater.

questions.text: Answer ANY FOUR of the following five questions, in about 50 words each.

subparts.text: i. Which qualities make the people of Coorg special? Answer with reference to the lesson. (Glimpses of India) [3]
subparts.answer: The people of Coorg are a proud, martial race known for their courage and bravery. Coorgi homes have a tradition of hospitality. They are possibly of Greek or Arabic descent, and they are the only people in India allowed to carry firearms without a licence. The Coorg Regiment is among the most decorated in the Indian Army.

subparts.text: ii. Why does the poet say that only God could love Anne Gregory for herself alone? (For Anne Gregory) [3]
subparts.answer: The young man in the poem loves Anne only for her yellow hair, and she wishes to be loved for herself. The poet suggests, through an old religious man, that no young man can love her without being attracted by her looks. Only God can love her for herself alone, apart from outward beauty.

subparts.text: iii. What did Nelson Mandela learn about courage, and from whom? (Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom) [3]
subparts.answer: Mandela learnt the meaning of courage from his comrades in the struggle. Time and again he saw men and women risk their lives for an idea and stand up to attack and torture without breaking. He learnt that courage is not the absence of fear but the triumph over it. The brave man is one who conquers his fear.

subparts.text: iv. Which factors helped Richard Ebright to become a scientist? (The Making of a Scientist) [3]
subparts.answer: Ebright was curious and determined from childhood and began collecting butterflies in kindergarten. His mother encouraged him by buying telescopes, microscopes and cameras, and by getting him the book The Travels of Monarch X. He then tagged and raised monarch butterflies for Dr Urquhart's research, which taught him to do real scientific work.

subparts.text: v. What lesson did Kisa Gotami learn from her search for a mustard seed? (The Sermon at Benares) [3]
subparts.answer: Kisa Gotami was mad with grief at her only son's death. The Buddha asked for a mustard seed from a house where no one had lost a child, husband, parent or friend. She went from house to house and could not find one. She realised that death is common to all and that her grief was selfish.

basis_question.text: Answer ANY TWO of the following three questions, in about 40-50 words.

subparts.text: How did Mr. Herriot treat Tricki at the hospital?
subparts.answer: Mr. Herriot made a bed for Tricki next to the other dogs' beds. He didn't give Tricki anything to eat for two days. He only gave it water. He was kept under keen observation and later given some exercise. Thus, Tricki gradually returned to his good health.

subparts.text:
Bholi's parents accepted the match for her though Bishamber Nath was nearly the same age as her father. Bholi also accepted her parents' decision without voicing her opinion.
i. What does this tell you about the social conditions prevailing in our society?
ii. How do you think these problems can be addressed?
subparts.answer: When Bishamber greedily demanded five thousand rupees as a condition to marry a girl with pock marks on her face, Bholi refused to allow him to garland her and told him that he was a contemptible person. These problems can be addressed if proper education is imparted to everyone in the society.

subparts.text: One should never judge a book by its cover. Explain with reference to Ausable and how he outwits Max with his presence of mind. (The Midnight Visitor)
subparts.answer: Ausable, despite appearing unimpressive and unlike a typical spy, demonstrates cleverness and quick thinking. He uses his calm demeanor and a fabricated story about a balcony to trick Max. When Henry, the waiter, knocks, Ausable pretends it's the police, causing Max to panic and escape through a nonexistent balcony, showcasing Ausable's sharp intellect.

questions.text: Answer ANY TWO of the following three questions, in about 40-50 words.

subparts.text: How did Mrs Pumphrey's love for Tricki nearly harm him? How was he brought back to health? (A Triumph of Surgery)
subparts.answer: Mrs Pumphrey overfed Tricki with cream cakes and chocolates and gave him little exercise, so he became hugely fat and listless. Mr Herriot took him to his surgery, gave him no food but plenty of water for two days, and let him play with the other dogs. Soon Tricki regained his health.

subparts.text: How was Horace Danby trapped by the young lady? (A Question of Trust)
subparts.answer: The young lady pretended to be the lady of the house and said she had forgotten the numbers of the safe. Horace took off his gloves to give her his lighter, opened the safe and handed over the jewels. She was a thief herself. His fingerprints were all over the house, so the police arrested him for the jewel robbery.

subparts.text: How did school change Bholi? Mention two changes. (Bholi)
subparts.answer: Bholi was a timid girl who stammered and was neglected at home. Her kind teacher encouraged her patiently and she learnt to speak without fear. She gained confidence and self-respect. Later she courageously refused to marry a greedy man and decided to teach in the same school and serve her parents.

questions.text:
Answer any one of the following two questions, in about 100-120 words.

A. In 'The Black Aeroplane', the narrator is saved by an aeroplane that nobody else has seen. How does the author build mystery and suspense in the story?
questions.answer: Marking: Content-3, Expression-2, Accuracy-1. Value points: The story begins with a calm, easy night flight, so the sudden danger comes as a shock. The narrator takes a risk and flies into the huge, black storm clouds because he did not have enough fuel to fly around them. Inside the clouds, the compass and the radio go dead and he is lost, which creates tension. Then another aeroplane without lights appears and the pilot waves to him to follow. The mysterious aeroplane leads him to a runway when his last tank is nearly empty, and then it vanishes. The woman in the control centre says that no other aeroplane was flying and only his was on the radar. The story ends with unanswered questions, leaving the reader wondering who saved him.

or.text: B. Valli's first ride in the bus is a mixture of joy and sadness. With reference to 'Madam Rides the Bus', discuss how her experience on the journey changes her.
or.answer: Marking: Content-3, Expression-2, Accuracy-1. Value points: Valli is an eight-year-old girl who is curious about the bus that passes her village. She saves stray coins patiently and finally travels alone to the town. She is proud of her independence and insists on being treated as a grown-up when the conductor teases her as 'madam'. On the way she enjoys the sights from the window and laughs heartily when a young cow runs in front of the bus. On the return trip she sees the same cow lying dead by the roadside, and she is overcome with sadness and no longer wants to look out of the window. The thoughtless joy of the first trip is replaced by pity and a mature understanding of the cruelty and suffering in life, so the journey makes her more sensitive and grown-up.

questions.note: Attempt any ONE of A / B. A covers Ch03 (The Black Aeroplane); B covers Ch07.

questions.text:
Answer any one of the following two questions, in about 100-120 words.

A. Mathilde Loisel lost ten years of her life because of her pride and discontent. With reference to 'The Necklace', discuss how her attitude to life led to her downfall and what lesson the story gives.
questions.answer: Marking: Content-3, Expression-2, Accuracy-1. Value points: Mathilde is unhappy with her ordinary life and dreams of wealth and luxury, though her husband loves her and tries to please her. To look rich at the ball she borrows a diamond necklace from her friend Mme Forestier. When she loses it, her pride stops her from telling her friend the truth. She and her husband spend thirty-six thousand francs on a replacement, borrowing heavily. They live in poverty for ten years, working hard to repay the debt, and she grows old and coarse. At last she learns that the original necklace was only paste, worth not more than five hundred francs. The story teaches us to be content with what life gives us, to be honest, and not to value show over real worth.

or.text: B. Griffin had made a great scientific discovery, yet it brought him only trouble. With reference to 'Footprints without Feet', discuss why invisibility did not make him happy.
or.answer: Marking: Content-3, Expression-2, Accuracy-1. Value points: Griffin is a brilliant scientist who discovers how to become invisible, but he is a lawless and quick-tempered man. After he sets fire to his landlord's house, he has to remove his clothes to escape and becomes a homeless, penniless wanderer in the bitter cold of mid-winter. He breaks into a big London store for warmth and clothes, and later robs a shopkeeper and attacks him. At Iping he takes money from the clergyman's desk and frightens the villagers with moving furniture. He is chased by the assistants and finally by the constable. His invisibility brings him fear, loneliness and crime rather than happiness. The story shows that a scientific discovery misused without responsibility can become a curse.
